A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSLA study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original attention-head analyses, ablations, input perturbations, steering experiments, and generation results across six language models, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds semantic-subspace tests, threshold sensitivity analyses, attention and layer-dynamics analyses, composite-task experiments, and SubjQA generation results.

M1.justification: The TR projection-norm score, normalized TL logit-gap score, head-ranking procedure, and task-vector construction and injection remain unchanged. The added tasks apply the existing procedure; expanded explanations and revised notation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds Country–Capital plus Antonym composite ICL in Appendix H.4 and book-review generation using SubjQA with human-written reviews and a richer sentiment-label space in Appendix I.3. These extend v1's seven classification datasets and synthetic binary movie reviews to sequential constituent tasks and more varied generation.

E2.justification: DLA-based head identification, induction heads, random heads, and the relevant ICL and zero-shot reference conditions remain in their corresponding comparisons. SubjQA extends the existing task-vector comparison set. The new random-subspace contrast tests an assumption rather than introducing a competing head-identification method.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a 1–10% head-selection sweep, equal-sized random-vocabulary subspace controls, attention-mass and layerwise logit-margin measurements, and position-specific composite-task ablations using 10% of heads in one direction and 3% in the other. These supplement rather than replace the retained eight-shot experiments and default 3% threshold.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct tests of the shared semantic-subspace premise, sensitivity of ablation and steering to head-selection thresholds, aggregate attention distributions and individual prompt traces, and analyses explaining why TL heads occur earlier than TR heads. Composite-task cross-ablation also tests whether TR transfers across subtasks while TL remains specialized.

E5.justification: Appendix F and Table 5 introduce Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for paired semantic-versus-random projection norms. V1 already reported Mann–Whitney tests for layer distributions and means with standard deviations for generation ratings. V2 does not state an increase in repeated runs or introduce seed counts.

E6.justification: The earlier figure results and layer-statistics table values are retained, while substantial new results are added. Table 4 reports cross-subtask Spearman correlations of 0.8365 for TR heads versus 0.2980 for TL heads; Figure 53 shows TR-vector accuracy increasing up to roughly 7% head selection. Figures 100–105 add SubjQA ratings, although Figures 100 and 102 repeat an identical plot under different model captions.

T1.justification: V2 removes the unsupported assertion that Equation 3's TL score lies in [-1,1] and qualifies the random-set Jaccard expression as asymptotic. Theorem 1 and its Appendix B proof are unchanged. The revised row-oriented unembedding dimensions also introduce an inconsistency with the unchanged projector formula near Equation 2.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims: TSLA localizes separable TR/TL functions, TR promotes task-subspace alignment, TL promotes within-subspace discrimination, and the framework explains induction heads and task vectors. The new contribution list summarizes existing claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 explains the earlier occurrence of TL heads through the distinction between within-task discrimination and task-versus-nontask separation. It adds interpretations of query-versus-label attention and shared TR versus specialized TL mechanisms in composite tasks. It also discusses task vectors' single-token scope and explicitly motivates broader generation tests by acknowledging the synthetic movie task's simplicity.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised future code release with a code-implementation repository link. It documents the new semantic-token set, threshold sweep, composite prompts and intervention positions, and SubjQA book split and rating procedure. Existing hardware, quantization, sample limits, prompt templates, and steering recipes remain unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bjerva et al. (2020) for SubjQA and Li et al. (2025), whose findings motivate the composite-task discussion in Appendix H.4. It removes Li et al. (2024) and Marks and Tegmark (2024). Related work more explicitly connects prior approaches to individual experiments, while the overarching research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 adds an explicit contribution list, organizes related work with thematic paragraph headings, and revises method explanations and experimental transitions. Appendix organization expands, and publication headers and affiliations change. The overall main-section sequence and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds main-text attention-distribution and token-attention figures, extensive appendix plots for the new analyses and tasks, and two new results tables. Existing figures are retained and reflowed, while the layer-statistics tables are grouped near the end. These are substantial additions to the visual evidence, beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V1 offered limited direct checks of the semantic-subspace premise and fixed 3% selection threshold, and its generation evidence used synthetic binary movie reviews. V2 adds targeted controls, threshold sweeps, layer-order explanations, and composite and human-written review tasks, substantially strengthening support for the retained framework. These gains outweigh localized problems: the unexplained duplicate SubjQA plots in Figures 100 and 102 and the matrix-dimension inconsistency near Equation 2.
